entry.evidence: The new in situ geodynamic laboratory established in the framework of the ICDP Eger project aims to develop the most modern, comprehensive, multiparameter laboratory at [...]

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), checked against the published PDF

steps.action: States the open questions on the processes behind earthquake activity and fluid mobility, crustal fluid pathways, and the influence of geological processes on the deep biosphere.
steps.quote: These are the open questions tackled by the ICDP project aimed at drilling in the Eger Rift region.

steps.action: Adopts from the literature the working hypothesis that swarm seismicity reflects fault reactivation triggered by ascending magmatic fluids through CO2 conduits.
steps.quote: triggered by the ascent of magmatic fluids caused by ongoing magmatic process

steps.action: Reports from the authors' earlier surface-network work that surface recordings lose high-frequency detail to near-surface damping and scattering.
steps.quote: they suffer from high-frequency wave damping by the near-surface weathered layers and site scattering

steps.action: Designs monitoring at a few hundred meters depth to avoid high-frequency attenuation and resolve low-magnitude events, exploiting the regular recurrence of swarms at known spots.
steps.quote: A monitoring depth of a few hundred meters will avoid high-frequency attenuation

steps.action: Cites decades of repeated surface fluid probing, including 3He/4He trend changes, and judges these data insufficient for the objectives.
steps.quote: However, the data obtained have not been sufficient to reach the objectives.

steps.action: Specifies the laboratory concept of borehole 3-D seismic arrays plus continuous real-time multi-depth fluid monitoring, as developed at the 2013 ICDP workshop (Dahm et al., 2013).
steps.quote: such a laboratory comprises the novel concept of 3-D seismic arrays with a set of shallow boreholes

steps.action: Uses published reflection imaging, local earthquake tomography, magnetotellurics and attenuation tomography that infer an intrusive body and fluid pathways beneath the NK focal zone.
steps.quote: Local earthquake tomography showed clear indications of a mid-crustal intrusive body beneath the NK focal zone

steps.action: Selects drill sites around the NK focal zone and at the Hartoušov mofette using local resistivity tomography, reflection/refraction seismics and noise measurements to control waveform quality and SNR.
steps.quote: The exact positions of the drill holes were investigated by local geophysical surveying to control the quality of waveforms

steps.action: Drills, cores, cases, redrills and cements the boreholes through blowout preventers under contamination control, with well logging of all sites except S2.
steps.quote: Some innovative approaches were applied during drilling and subsequent logging to meet the specific requirements of multidisciplinary research.

steps.action: Builds the seismological boreholes S1-S3 as vertical borehole arrays combined with surface small-aperture arrays, targeting events of ML > -1 at 1 kHz sampling in unaltered rock.
steps.quote: Boreholes S1–S3 involve deploying vertical seismic arrays combined with a surface small-aperture high-frequency array

steps.action: Checks site suitability with a test array and test measurements in the Bad Brambach hole (S1), a test-array noise characterization (S2), and long-term WEBNET station STC monitoring (S3).
steps.quote: test measurements in the nearby Bad Brambach 80 m hole indicated the appropriate site conditions and excellent signal-to-noise ratios

steps.action: Drills S4 into the newly discovered Bažina maar through sediments and basaltoids into granite, planning a bottom-hole seismometer where a pre-site survey indicated good SNR.
steps.quote: a bottom-hole seismometer is planned to be deployed in the solid granitic rocks at the bottom of the hole

steps.action: Builds the multilevel gas monitoring system in boreholes F1-F3 at the Hartoušov mofette, with on-site seismometers and a weather station, and a planned capillary tube for fresh deep gas.
steps.quote: The multilevel gas monitoring system is being installed at three wells tapping the CO 2 horizons at 20, 65 and 229 m.

steps.action: Measures radon continuously while drilling F3, locates a CO2 horizon and perforates the casing there; hydraulic tests to confirm the perforation are still pending.
steps.quote: [...] while drilling revealed a promising CO 2 horizon, which was later chosen for perforations of the steel casing.

steps.action: Reports pilot-hole F2 results from Bussert et al. (2017), with co-authors in common: a CO2 blowout indicating a pathway, mineral-water chemistry and first microbiological tests; F3 microbial analyses are ongoing.
steps.quote: The drilling through a thin caprock-like structure triggered a CO 2 blowout, indicating a CO 2 pathway.

steps.action: Presents depth-matched well logs and stratigraphy for S1 and S3 and a stratigraphy-only profile for S2, identifying fractured intervals and lithology changes.
steps.quote: All logs show a constant trend except at two main fractured intervals

steps.action: Estimates heat flow (75 to >100 mW m-2) from temperature logs, using 3-D topographic corrections and optically scanned thermal conductivity with anisotropy assessed.
steps.quote: Based on the above, we calculated the heat flow

steps.action: Builds the S1 pilot array: a 10-level 3C HG-7 geophone chain and a bottom-hole ASIR SiA broadband seismometer at 1 kHz, plus a three-ring surface array of 4.5 Hz geophones with near-real-time transmission.
steps.quote: We identified 10 Hz HG-7 geophones as the optimum sensors

steps.action: Checks the borehole chain on an ML 0.1 microearthquake recorded during the 8-level test installation, showing good SNR that improves with depth relative to the surface sensor.
steps.quote: Note the good signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) of the recordings and their improvement with depth.

steps.action: Installs a strain-sensing single-mode fiber-optic cable behind the S1 casing to 397.5 m, with separators to improve cement coupling, for microearthquake monitoring and cement control.
steps.quote: After drilling S1, a fiber-optic cable was installed behind the casing down to a depth of 397.5 m

steps.action: Verifies cable integrity by optical time-domain reflectometry before cementing, then monitors cementation by distributed fiber-optic strain (OFDR, Luna OBR 4400) every 60 s for 2 h.
steps.quote: The quality of cementation was controlled by the distributed fiber-optic strain measurements along the cable

steps.action: Plans data management by computing the expected data volume (16 GB per day per 3-D array, about 180 TB over 10 years) and transmission via 4G and SeedLink.
steps.quote: This sums to 50 GB d - 1 (including S4)

steps.action: Keeps the status claim that all monitoring boreholes are drilled, S1 is instrumented and fluid monitoring is in a pilot phase, and expects increased monitoring sensitivity.
steps.quote: Seismic instrumenting has been completed in the S1 borehole and is under preparation at the four remaining monitoring borehole sites

tree.answer: Yes: fluid-related earthquake swarms and mantle-derived CO2 degassing are established in the literature
Partly: swarms are recorded at the surface, but source processes and fluid pathways are not observed directly; surface records lose high frequencies
Build a multiparameter borehole observatory (seismic arrays, multi-depth fluid monitoring, deep biosphere)
No rivals stated; one working hypothesis (fluid-triggered swarms)
Conditions found: sites selected around the NK focal zone and at the Hartoušov mofette

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: swarms recur regularly at known spots with known radiation patterns
Site SNR tests, the depth-improvement waveform example and cementation checks support the capability; no performance metrics are given
Capability partly established and characterized; scientific questions deferred
Reviewed by two anonymous referees; no review file supplied

end.claim: All five monitoring boreholes of the Eger Rift observatory have been drilled, cored and largely logged, and the S1 pilot 3-D high-frequency array is operating and records microearthquakes with good SNR that improves with depth; instrumentation at the other sites is in preparation.

decisive_move.sentence: Drilling, casing, cementing and instrumenting the shallow boreholes (above all the S1 pilot 3-D array) creates the observatory, without which no claim exists.

gates.evidence: The fluid-triggered-swarm hypothesis (§1 ¶5) and recurring swarm locations (§2 ¶2) guided site placement around NK and at the mofette, but no hypothesis is tested. The main claim is a status report on a built facility, supported only by site SNR tests and one example event (Figure 12), with no test it could have failed. The design concept and the technical target of analyzing ML > -1 events were fixed before drilling at the 2013 workshop (Dahm et al., 2013; §2 ¶6, §4.3 ¶1); no analysis plan or threshold for results was preregistered.

imports.item: Optical frequency domain reflectometry (Froggatt and Moore, 1998) and optical time-domain reflectometry for distributed strain sensing and cable integrity
Blowout preventer, drilling rigs and casing cementation practices
DNA extraction, cultivation experiments and methane-production activity tests on core samples
Data transmission via 4G mobile standard to an open VPN server with SeedLink

novelty_claims.quote: aims to develop the most modern, comprehensive, multiparameter laboratory at [...]
A modern, comprehensive, high-resolution observatory at depth with unique multiparameter observation can interconnect fields of primary research
analyzing the fluid-induced source processes and the anatomy of earthquake swarms and their migration in unprecedented detail
such a laboratory comprises the novel concept of 3-D seismic arrays with a set of shallow boreholes
an innovative approach using a fiber-optic cable was additionally applied to monitor the cementing at S1
in a newly discovered volcanic maar structure penetrating the surrounding granitic rocks
The bottom-hole equipment consists of a newly developed ASIR SiA broadband seismometer

limits: This is a Science Report on an observatory under construction, and no scientific question posed in §1 is answered. No rivals are stated, and the fluid-triggering hypothesis is cited, not tested. Capability characterization is thin: one example event (Figure 12) and qualitative SNR statements, with no detection threshold, noise spectra or location accuracy reported; the target of ML > -1 is stated but not demonstrated. Sub-claims: heat flow of 75 to >100 mW m-2 (§6 ¶1) is an estimate_with_resolution in kind but is given without uncertainty; the fracture zones in the S1 and S3 logs are observations without a status. The F3 perforation success is unconfirmed (§4.5 ¶1), F3 microbial results are pending (§4.5 ¶4), and S4 and F3 logs are deferred to other studies (§5 ¶1). The S2 core is not available, and S2 was not logged. The entry could also be read as 'problem', since the open questions open §1; it is coded 'capability' because the paper's own work is building the facility (coder's judgment). A review statement records two anonymous referees, but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. Whether the site-suitability tests were performed by the authors or by contractors is inferred, not stated.

disagreements.target: Systematic surface fluid probing at springs and mofettes (Weise et al., 2001; Bräuer et al., 2003, 2005a, b, 2008, 2014; [...]
disagreements.support: The paper argues that repeated surface sampling cannot separate surface from deep effects and proposes continuous multi-depth monitoring; it offers no new data comparing the two.
disagreements.quote: However, the data obtained have not been sufficient to reach the objectives.

disagreements.target: Surface earthquake recordings of the existing network (e.g., Fischer et al., 2014)
disagreements.support: Surface records are said to lose high-frequency detail; the borehole waveform example showing SNR improving with depth (Figure 12) is the only evidence offered.
disagreements.quote: they suffer from high-frequency wave damping by the near-surface weathered layers and site scattering

alternatives_considered.chosen: Borehole monitoring at a few hundred meters depth
alternatives_considered.reason: Avoid high-frequency attenuation and site scattering in near-surface weathered layers

alternatives_considered.chosen: Seismic sites in unaltered crystalline rock not affected by fluid ascent
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Sites in fluid-altered or sedimentary ground (implied)
alternatives_considered.reason: Assures recording of high-frequency signals of the smallest earthquakes

alternatives_considered.chosen: 10 Hz HG-7 geophones, paired in series
alternatives_considered.reason: Little or no tilt sensitivity, high spurious and low corner frequencies, large usable bandwidth; series pairs increase output voltage

alternatives_considered.chosen: CO2 horizon found by continuous radon measurement for casing perforation in F3
alternatives_considered.reason: Radon measurements revealed a promising CO2 horizon

alternatives_considered.chosen: PVC liners for F3 cores; aluminum encapsulation for S4 cores
alternatives_considered.reason: Protection from biological contamination; no reason given for the different choices

alternatives_considered.chosen: Seismic sensor in P1 deemed questionable
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Deploying a high-frequency seismic sensor in the maar borehole
alternatives_considered.reason: Pre-site survey indicates shallow maar sedimentary successions are unsuitable for high-frequency seismic monitoring

alternatives_considered.chosen: S2 instrumentation same as S1 except for the fiber-optic cable
